# Independent audit: actual depth-root failure inside the Minkowski section



The actual three-fiber hull has exactly the specified planar fibers because the endpoint Minkowski average is contained in the middle triangle. The body is full-dimensional, all three fibers have positive area, and the exact masses are \(1/2,49/32,2\), totaling \(129/32\). The largest is strictly below half the total. The explicit witnesses prove that the middle and large endpoint bodies are not nested.

Every candidate \(y_t=(t,t)\), \(0<t\le1/3\), is strictly inside the endpoint Minkowski section. The same simplex \(L_t=3tT\) lies in both endpoints and has centroid \(y_t\). The proved paired-tail theorem therefore supplies \(4t^2\) for every oblique endpoint pair. Separately, the shifted simplex \(E_t=(-\delta,-\delta)+3(t+\delta)T\) lies in the middle body and has that same centroid, giving \(2(t+\delta)^2\) by ordinary Grünbaum. The containment constants are valid throughout the entire stated interval. Purely base-normal caps retain at least the same bounds.

The single cap \(x_1+x_2\le2t\) matches the sum exactly. Its endpoint traces are both \(2tT\), and its middle trace is \((-\delta,-\delta)+2(t+\delta)T\). All are proper triangles. Thus the profile is the actual all-halfspace minimum at each candidate, rather than a selected-orientation upper bound alone.

The three rational values \(11/128,24/128,43/128\) are correct. The proposed square-root midpoint inequality is equivalent to \(441\ge473\), so it fails strictly. The calculation \(2PP''-(P')^2=32\delta^2>0\) also gives strict convexity of the square root along the segment.

The separate safe point is rigorously certified. The middle body contains \(D\), whose centroid is \((1/2,1/2)\) and whose Grünbaum cap bound is \(1/2\). Reflection in that point maps the small endpoint triangle into the large endpoint triangle. Pairing corresponding points therefore supplies another \(1/2\) in every endpoint cap pair. Vertical cuts only add full-fiber mass. The resulting absolute bound \(1>43/48\) exceeds the OC target.

This is a valid failure of root concavity for the full three-layer source, even inside the endpoint Minkowski section. It leaves the endpoint-only root-concavity theorem and its sum-of-two-powers motion bound intact, and it is not an OC counterexample.
